{{Short description|Statistical measure of dispersion}}

'''Morisita's overlap index''', named after [[Masaaki Morisita]], is a [[dispersion (statistics)|statistical measure of dispersion]] of individuals in a population.  It is used to compare overlap among [[Sample (statistics)|samples]] (Morisita 1959).  This formula is based on the assumption that increasing the size of the samples will increase the diversity because it will include different habitats (i.e. different faunas).

Formula:

: <math>C_D= \frac{2\sum_{i=1}^S x_i y_i }{(D_x + D_y) XY }</math>

: ''x''<sub>''i''</sub> is the number of times species ''i'' is represented in the total ''X'' from one sample.
: ''y''<sub>''i''</sub> is the number of times species ''i'' is represented in the total ''Y'' from another sample.
: ''D''<sub>''x''</sub> and ''D''<sub>''y''</sub> are the [[Simpson's index]] values for the ''x'' and ''y'' samples respectively.
: ''S'' is the number of unique species

''C''<sub>''D''</sub> = 0 if the two samples do not overlap in terms of species, and ''C''<sub>''D''</sub> = 1 if the species occur in the same proportions in both samples.{{citation needed|date=February 2012}}

Horn's modification of the index is (Horn 1966):
:<math>C_H= \frac{ 2 \sum_{i=1}^S x_i y_i }{ \left( {\sum_{i=1}^S x_i^2 \over X^2} + {\sum_{i=1}^S y_i^2 \over Y^2} \right) X Y } \,.</math>

Note, not to be confused with [[Taylor's law#Morisita’s index of dispersion|Morisita’s index of dispersion]].

== As probabilities/frequencies ==

If the population frequencies are defined as

: <math>p_i = x_i / X</math>
: <math>q_i = y_i / Y</math>

Then <math>D_x = \sum_{i=1}^S p_i^2</math> and <math>D_y = \sum_{i=1}^S q_i^2</math>, and the formula can be refactored as

: <math>C_D = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^S p_i q_i}
                   {\frac{1}{2}(\sum_{i=1}^S p_i^2 + \sum_{i=1}^S q_i^2)}</math>

which reveals a relationship to the [[Cosine similarity]], but normalizes the [[dot product]] by the arithmetic means instead of geometric means of the frequency vector squared lengths.
